pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. went

3. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.

4. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

6. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

7. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.

8. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

9. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. blue
   D. happiness

11. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.

12. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

2. D — went

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

5. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

6. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

10. A — run

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pre-Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Handwriting; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
